from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Words convert into high-dimensional numerical vectors.",
            "Similar words cluster closely in semantic space.",
            "'Cat' and 'Dog' appear nearby.",
            "'Airplane' remains far from animals."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Concept of Word Embeddings", lecture_lines)
        
        # Prepare semantic points
        cat = Dot(color=BLUE).scale(1.5)
        dog = Dot(color=BLUE).scale(1.5)
        airplane = Dot(color=YELLOW).scale(1.5)
        
        cat_label = Text("Cat", font_size=20)
        dog_label = Text("Dog", font_size=20)
        airplane_label = Text("Airplane", font_size=20)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Words convert into high-dimensional numerical vectors.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        vec_display = Tex(r"$\vec{v}_{word} = [0.1, -0.5, 0.8, \dots]$", font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(vec_display, 'B3')
        self.play(FadeIn(vec_display))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Similar words cluster closely in semantic space.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#808080"))
        # Using simple markers to simulate semantic map
        cluster_area = Rectangle(width=3, height=3, color=GRAY, stroke_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(cluster_area, 'C2', 'E5')
        self.play(FadeIn(cluster_area))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # 'Cat' and 'Dog' appear nearby.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.place_at_grid(cat, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(dog, 'D4')
        self.place_at_grid(cat_label, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(dog_label, 'D5')
        self.play(FadeIn(cat), FadeIn(dog), FadeIn(cat_label), FadeIn(dog_label))
        
        distance_line = Line(cat.get_center(), dog.get_center(), color=RED)
        self.play(Create(distance_line))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(distance_line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # 'Airplane' remains far from animals.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.place_at_grid(airplane, 'E2')
        self.place_at_grid(airplane_label, 'F2')
        self.play(FadeIn(airplane), FadeIn(airplane_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Core Innovation: Self-Attention Mechanism", [
            "Transformers analyze entire sentences simultaneously.",
            "Self-attention calculates relevance scores between words.",
            "Context depends on other sentence words.",
            "'It' links to 'animal' in context.",
            "Final attention weights visualization."
        ])
        
        words = ["The", "animal", "didn't", "cross", "the", "street", "because", "it", "was", "too", "tired"]
        word_mobs = VGroup(*[Text(w, font_size=24) for w in words]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(word_mobs, "B1", "B6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(word_mobs))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Visualize attention as paths
        it_idx = 7
        animal_idx = 1
        line = Line(word_mobs[it_idx].get_top(), word_mobs[animal_idx].get_top(), color=YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        rect = SurroundingRectangle(word_mobs, color=GREEN, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        dot = Dot(color="#FF00FF").next_to(word_mobs[it_idx], UP)
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(word_mobs[animal_idx].get_top() + UP*0.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Transformer Architecture", [
            "Encoders process and understand input text.", 
            "Decoders generate outputs token-by-token."
        ])
        
        # Elements for the animation
        encoder_block = Rectangle(width=2, height=3, color=WHITE).set_fill(opacity=0.3)
        decoder_block = Rectangle(width=2, height=3, color=WHITE).set_fill(opacity=0.3)
        encoder_label = Text("Encoder", font_size=20).next_to(encoder_block, UP)
        decoder_label = Text("Decoder", font_size=20).next_to(decoder_block, UP)
        
        encoder_group = VGroup(encoder_block, encoder_label)
        decoder_group = VGroup(decoder_block, decoder_label)
        
        self.place_at_grid(encoder_group, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(decoder_group, 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(encoder_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(decoder_group))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # Show flow
        flow_arrow = Arrow(encoder_group.get_right(), decoder_group.get_left(), color=BLUE)
        self.play(Create(flow_arrow))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Practical Application: Next-Token Prediction", [
            "Models predict the next likely token.",
            "They function as advanced probability engines.",
            "Visualizing the selection process."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        prompt = Text("The sky is...", font_size=36)
        token_box = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color=WHITE)

        # Position initial state
        self.place_at_grid(prompt, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(token_box, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.wait(1)

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Probability representation
        dist_box = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=2.0, color=YELLOW).set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(dist_box, 'C3', 'E5')
        self.play(FadeIn(dist_box))
        self.wait(1)

        self.place_at_grid(result, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(result))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Large Language Models and the Transformer Architecture
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic background in computer science or programming

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Word Embeddings
sections.content: Before understanding Transformers, we must represent language mathematically. Words are converted into high-dimensional vectors (embeddings) where similar words are closer together in space.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'semantic map' where 'Cat' and 'Dog' are plotted as nearby coordinate points, while 'Airplane' is far away.

sections.title: The Core Innovation: Self-Attention Mechanism
sections.content: Explain how Transformers look at the entire sentence simultaneously. The Attention mechanism calculates a 'relevance score' between each word and every other word in the sequence, allowing the model to understand context.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired,' visual lines (attention weights) connect 'it' specifically to 'animal' rather than 'street'.

sections.title: The Transformer Architecture: Encoder and Decoder
sections.content: Introduce the Encoder-Decoder stack. The Encoder 'reads and understands' the input, while the Decoder 'generates' the output token-by-token. Use a diagram showing data flowing through layers.
sections.example: An animation showing a 'Translator Robot' reading an English input block, compressing it into abstract meaning, and then generating a Japanese output block.

sections.title: Scaling to Large Language Models (LLMs)
sections.content: Explain that an LLM is essentially a massive Transformer trained on a colossal amount of data. Emphasize that 'Large' refers to both the number of parameters and the size of the training corpus.
sections.example: Representing a small model as a light bulb and an LLM as a vast city power grid, illustrating the jump in reasoning capability and knowledge breadth.

sections.title: Practical Application: Next-Token Prediction
sections.content: Conclude by showing how these models function: they are probability engines that predict the most likely next word in a sequence based on all previous tokens.
sections.example: A 'Predictive Slot Machine' animation where the prompt 'The sky is...' results in the model rolling symbols until it selects 'blue' with the highest probability.
